findings.label: Interceptor reacts to 401 only, not 403
findings.detail: The brief phrased the trigger as '401/403-unauthenticated', but the axios interceptor redirects only on a 401 for a request that carried a bearer header and leaves 403 alone. This is the correct authn/authz split: a 403 is a permission denial on a valid session (e.g. study membership/scope), and clearing the token on it would wrongly log the user out. No change required; recorded so the deviation from the brief's wording is explicit.

findings.label: No automated test for the auth guard or interceptor redirect
findings.detail: The _app beforeLoad guard and the interceptor redirect have no new unit/router test in this commit; only the cursor-accumulator fix is covered by a new suite. Both paths are small and verified by manual reasoning plus existing login tests, so this is acceptable, but a router-level test asserting the unauthenticated bounce and redirect-param round-trip would harden it.
